LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines two sources: a prebuilt Arch package from the ungoogled-chromium GitHub releases and a Google Chrome `.deb` package from Google's official domain (`dl.google.com`). Both are standard binary sources, and their checksums are explicitly provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloads will be verified during fetch.

The global scope contains only variable assignments and array definitions — no command substitutions, function calls, or immediate executions. The `pkgver()` function is absent, so no dynamic version computation occurs. The `prepare()`, `package()`, and `check()` functions are defined but will not be executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags. Therefore, no code that manipulates or extracts files runs during this phase.

Fetching and sourcing this PKGBUILD with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` is safe. It will only download the two binaries using verified URLs and parse the metadata, with no execution of extracted content or untrusted code.
</details>
<summary>
No active code in sourcing phase; sources are verified and standard.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD retrieves two sources: a prebuilt Arch Linux package for ungoogled-chromium and the official Google Chrome `.deb` package from dl.google.com. The latter is used solely to extract the WidevineCdm component, which is then injected into the final package under `/usr/lib/chromium/`. This is consistent with the package's purpose of providing Widevine support in an otherwise de-Googled browser.

The build process involves unpacking binaries using standard tools (bsdtar, tar), copying files into the package directory, setting appropriate permissions on `chrome-sandbox`, and validating that required Widevine files exist and have no missing dynamic dependencies via `ldd`. All operations are transparent, use well-known commands, and stay within expected packaging workflows. The sources are fetched over HTTPS from trusted domains (github.com and dl.google.com), and checksums are provided and match standard practice.

There is no code execution, network activity at runtime, obfuscation, or exfiltration. The script does not modify system files outside the package directory, nor does it install backdoors or execute arbitrary downloads. Extracting components from official vendor packages to add functionality (like DRM) is a known and accepted practice in the AUR ecosystem. No malicious or suspicious behavior is present.
</details>
<summary>
No malicious behavior; standard AUR packaging practices used
</summary>
</security_assessment>
